title: Product Comparison Video: Side by Side | AIVideosUGC
description: Help shoppers choose between your colors, sizes or sets with a side-by-side comparison video. One photo of both becomes a clip for listings or Shorts.
h1: Make a Product Comparison Video of Your Own Options
lead: Shoppers who cannot tell your colors, sizes or sets apart leave without buying, and text specs rarely settle it. Upload one photo showing both options and get a product comparison video that demonstrates the real difference so customers can choose with confidence.
benefits_h2: Why make a product comparison video?

benefits.d: A moving side-by-side view shows size, finish or included pieces more clearly than a spec line. Buyers can see which option fits their need instead of opening a support chat or leaving.
One source photo with both options supplies a shared scale and light. You demonstrate a full range without staging each color or size in front of a camera.
Choose 1:1 for a product gallery, 16:9 for a description embed or 9:16 for Shorts. Lengths run 6, 10, 15 or 30 seconds, so a simple pair and a detailed feature walkthrough both fit.

benefits.t: Exact labels stay under your control
benefits.d: Add variant names, measurements and prices as editable text after download. Your numbers stay accurate, and the finished clip carries no AIVideosUGC watermark.

intro: A comparison ad can help shoppers choose between two finishes, fits, or sizes. Show both options in one frame or have a creator explain the visible difference while holding them.

Comparison clips answer practical questions about color, size, fit and packaging. Show your own options together, then add variant names and current prices in an editable layer. Use 1:1, 16:9 or 9:16 for the placement you need.
tip: Photograph both options together and describe one visible difference, such as color, size, finish or included pieces.
steps_h2: How to make a product comparison video in 3 simple steps
steps_lead: Three steps turn one photo of both options into a clear side-by-side clip — no studio, no models, no reshoot.

steps.d: Photograph both options with full silhouettes, one angle and even light. A shared surface gives the clip an honest scale instead of a faked difference.
Name one difference, such as capacity, color, finish or included pieces, and the action that shows it. The clip proves it without a second shoot.
Add variant names, measurements and prices after download, then pick 1:1, 16:9 or 9:16 for the placement. The clip is ready with no AIVideosUGC watermark.

ideas.d: Stand your small and large bottles together so buyers see the real difference in height.
Show your updated design next to the previous one so returning customers recognize it.
Compare one item with your gift set to show which pieces come in the bundle.

faq.q: Can I compare my product with another brand's?
faq.a: No. Use this template to compare options from your own range, like two colors or two sizes. Requests that include other companies' logos or trademarks may be refused.

faq.q: Can the video show capacity, weight, or price?
faq.a: Add specs like these as text in your editor after downloading. Generated numbers aren't always accurate, so it's safer to type them yourself.

faq.q: Which aspect ratio should I choose?
faq.a: Square 1:1 works well in product galleries and feeds. Widescreen 16:9 suits a video in your product description. Vertical 9:16 is for YouTube Shorts and other phone-first feeds.

faq.q: Can the clip show measurements on screen?
faq.a: Numbers are added as a text layer after download so they stay exact. The clip can show both options side by side as you demonstrate them.
A 10-second clip usually covers both options; choose 15 seconds when each one needs a demonstration and 30 for both demos in full. Clips cost 24, 40, 60 or 120 credits for 6, 10, 15 or 30 seconds.

faq.q: Can I compare two of my own products?
faq.a: Yes. Upload both options together and describe which feature each side should show.

faq.q: Should both products be in one source photo?
faq.a: Yes. A single photo with both options fully visible gives the comparison a shared scale and light reference. Leave space between them, keep caps and bases inside the frame, and avoid props that could make one option look larger or more important than the other.

faq.q: Can I compare features instead of sizes?
faq.a: Yes. Compare a visible, supportable difference such as a finish, colorway, closure, included accessory, or capacity marking. Describe one action that reveals it, then add the exact feature name and any measurement as editable text after download.

faq.q: Can I use one source photo for both variants?
faq.a: Yes. One frame with both options fully visible gives the generator a shared scale and light reference, as long as both caps, bases, and edges stay inside the frame.

faq.q: How do I keep the two products at the same scale?
faq.a: Place both products on one level surface or hold them at equal height, leave space between them, and describe the shared camera distance. Add exact measurements later as editable text.

faq.q: Which variant should the comparison link to?
faq.a: Link to the product page that lists both options, then use the final text layer or CTA to name the tested size, finish, or color. Do not imply that one option is available if it is out of stock.

faq.q: Can I run this video as a paid ad?
faq.a: Yes. Videos you make can be used in your own ads, listings and social posts, with no AIVideosUGC watermark on the download. You remain responsible for your ad text, claims and platform disclosures.

faq.q: Is a 30-second clip worth it for two products?
faq.a: Use 30 seconds when each option needs its own demonstration, such as showing capacity on one side and included pieces on the other. For a single visible difference, 6 or 10 seconds is usually enough.

overview.h2: Compare what the camera can actually show
overview.d: A side-by-side clip is useful for color, size, finish, included pieces, or packaging. Keep the two items in one stable composition and let viewers inspect the difference; put performance claims and exact specifications in your product listing.

overview.h2: Keep the comparison about your range
overview.d: Use this template for your own variants, sizes, or bundles. It can clarify a choice without naming or implying a competing brand, and it leaves the final decision with the shopper.

input_guide.h2: Photograph both options for fair scale

items.d: Place both items on the same plain surface so the scene does not invent a scale difference.
Front views work for color and packaging; a three-quarter view can reveal a lid, handle, or side port on both products.
A small space between the options gives each label and silhouette room after the clip is downloaded.
Say charcoal versus cream, 12-ounce versus 20-ounce, or single item versus set instead of asking for a general comparison.
The clip can make color, form, packaging, or included pieces easy to inspect in one frame.
Use 1:1 for a listing or feed, 16:9 for a wide product section, or 9:16 for Stories and Reels.
Use current listing data for prices, capacities, dimensions and included pieces.
An adult creator holds a small and large bottle side by side, with both full silhouettes visible.
A creator holds matte black and brushed silver headphones at equal height.
Two creators wear charcoal and navy versions of the same legging cut in matched poses.
Show sage and blush cases together, each with one circular camera opening.

after_download.h2: Add facts the scene cannot show

items.d: Place the variant name, size, color, or model above the correct side.
Use current listing data for price, capacity, dimensions, and included pieces.
Describe the visible difference without adding a performance winner the clip cannot prove.

visual.overview: A comparison video helps a seller answer one visible shopping question: which size, finish, color, or package option is right for this customer? Upload both of your own options, describe the difference, and use the result on a [product page](/ai-video-generation/product-video), in a [Shorts placement](/platforms/youtube-shorts-ads), or alongside [Amazon product photos](/platforms/amazon-product-photos). Keep both products at a comparable scale, name each side in your editor, and do not use a generated comparison to make an unverified performance claim. A clear comparison is about the choice the shopper must make, not a general review.

steps.sourceTitle: Two sizes of an amber glass bottle
steps.sourceHint: Keep the small and large amber bottles, white droppers and blank labels fully visible.
steps.prompt: Use the uploaded pair as the exact options: one small and one large amber glass dropper bottle with white rubber bulbs, ribbed white caps and blank white labels. Preserve each bottle silhouette, cap and relative size. An adult creator holds one bottle in each hand beside her face and says, "Here are the two sizes side by side." She raises both equally and finishes with the full bottles facing the lens. Bright vanity daylight, natural skin texture. Chest-up front-facing handheld framing. Sound: her voice and two soft bottle taps; no music.

picker.title: Choose a product-comparison ad format
picker.lead: Choose a comparison scene that makes one buyer decision visible in the first seconds. Keep both options in one frame, match their scale, and use a side-by-side hold, fit check, or feature demonstration that your own product information can support. Use the prompt as a shot list: identify the two options, state the visible difference, then end with both products held still. Add a third option only in a separate version so the viewer does not lose track of the first two. Keep the pair in one visual system, use a matching camera distance, and let the product information you already publish decide which differences deserve a label. Use the product information you already publish to decide which differences deserve a label, and avoid unsupported performance claims in the comparison.
